tours.title: Tashkent tours to Amirsoy and Chimgan
tours.lead: Seven excursions we drive ourselves: four full days in the Western Tian Shan and three shorter ones inside Tashkent. Mountain routes leave at 9:00 and are back by 18:00, and every one of them runs in one Kia Sportage with the same driver from start to finish.
tours.section-title: Tours to Amirsoy and the Chimgan mountains
tours.section-lead: The Western Tian Shan begins about eighty kilometres from the centre of Tashkent, and the road there climbs through orchards, a river gorge and a turquoise reservoir before the ridges appear. Four mountain days, plus the metro, the plov centre and Magic City when you want a shorter one — no group buses, no fixed itinerary you have to keep up with.

catalog.title: Seven excursions we drive ourselves
catalog.lead: The four mountain routes all run on the same shape of day: pickup from wherever you are staying at 9:00, the climb up through Gazalkent into the Bostanlyk valleys, as long as you want at the destination, and back at your door by 18:00. The three city excursions are shorter — half a day for the metro and Besh Qozon, an evening for Magic City. Every route: up to four guests, one car, one driver who has done the road in every season.

hero.photo: Amirsoy gondola cabins crossing the Western Tian Shan ridges in late afternoon light.

practical.title: Practical notes before you book
practical.lead: The mountain routes run on the same day shape and the same car, so the only real decisions left to you are the date and the destination. The mountains around Tashkent change completely between seasons, and the difference between a good day and a cold one is usually a jacket and a start time. The three city excursions work in any weather. Here is everything we tell guests before they choose.
practical.season-caption: Best seasons for each mountain day trip from Tashkent

amirsoy.note: Snow and lifts from December, alpine meadows and trails from May

chimgan.note: Open meadows April to October, snow above 2,000 m from November

charvak.note: Warm enough to swim; clear air and empty shorelines the rest of the year

chinorkent.note: Glazed cabins in any weather; best on a clear day for the full circular view

metro.note: Entirely underground, so weather and season are irrelevant

plov.note: Go before 13:00 — when the kazan is finished, it is finished

magic-city.note: An evening route — the floodlights and the fountain show start after dark

schedule.pickup: 9:00 — the driver is at your apartment or hotel, no meeting point to find
schedule.drive: 9:00 to 10:30 — the climb through Gazalkent into the Bostanlyk valleys
schedule.arrival: 10:30 onwards — time at the destination at your pace, not on a group clock
schedule.lunch: Lunch wherever you prefer — a mountain cafe, a restaurant above the water, or one you bring
schedule.return: 18:00 — back at the door you were collected from
schedule.limit: Up to 9 hours in total; a later finish is possible if you agree it the day before
schedule.city: City excursions are three to four hours — morning or afternoon for the metro and Besh Qozon, after sunset for Magic City

drive.gazalkent: Gazalkent, the last town before the climb — about 50 minutes

bring.layers: Layers rather than one thick coat — the mountains run ten degrees colder than the city
bring.shoes: Shoes with grip for anything above the cable car stations
bring.sun: Sunglasses and sunscreen, the altitude is deceptive even in winter
bring.cash: Some cash in som for mountain cafes, lifts and lakeside restaurants
bring.water: A water bottle, refilled before you leave the apartment
bring.documents: A passport or ID, which some mountain resorts still ask to see

practical.car-lead: Every day trip and every transfer we run is driven in our own Kia Sportage. It is a compact SUV, which is the right car for this particular road: high enough for the mountain sections above Gazalkent, small enough to park at a crowded viewpoint, and comfortable enough that ninety minutes each way does not feel like the price of the day.

car.seats: Four passenger seats, so a family or two couples travel together in one car
car.climate: Air conditioning through the summer and a warm cabin on winter mornings
car.boot: Boot space for daypacks, ski gear or airport luggage on the way through
car.driver: The same driver all day, in Russian, Uzbek or English

practical.pickup-title: Pickup and where we collect you
practical.pickup: Every day trip begins wherever you are sleeping. If you are staying in one of our apartments in Tashkent city center the driver comes to the courtyard at the agreed time, and if you are in a hotel anywhere else in the city we collect you from the lobby at no extra cost. Guests arriving on an early flight often go straight from the airport into a mountain day with their luggage in the boot, which we are happy to arrange as part of the transfer.

amirsoy.title: Amirsoy mountain resort
amirsoy.summary: The newest mountain resort in Uzbekistan and the easiest full day in the mountains. Ninety minutes of driving through the Chirchik valley, then the whole middle of the day at 1,500 metres with terraces, trails, lifts and enough space to do nothing at all.
amirsoy.photo: The Amirsoy resort base under snow-dusted Western Tian Shan ridges on a clear winter morning, wooden chalet roofs and a lift line, pine forest climbing the slope behind, cool-neutral shadows against warm sunlit snow, no people in frame, 16:10 landscape.

photos.two: Amirsoy chalet village and chairlift beside a groomed winter piste under snow-covered ranges.

highlights.one: The climb through Gazalkent and the Bostanlyk orchards
highlights.two: Free time at the resort base — terraces, cafes and walking trails
highlights.three: Lifts and snow from December, alpine meadows from May

chimgan.title: Greater Chimgan
chimgan.summary: The classic Tashkent mountain day. Greater Chimgan rises to 3,309 metres above the Charvak basin, and the road to its foot hands you the whole Western Tian Shan skyline in a single afternoon — meadows and horses in summer, deep quiet snow in winter.
chimgan.photo: Greater Chimgan peak seen across a green alpine meadow in late spring, dramatic layered ridges receding into haze behind it, a dirt track curving through the grass, warm afternoon light, no people, 16:10 landscape.

photos.one: Alpenglow on the snow-covered summit of Greater Chimgan at dusk.
photos.two: Skiers and snowboarders on the open Chimgan slope beside the old drag lift.

highlights.one: The Chimgan plateau under the 3,309 m summit
highlights.two: Viewpoints looking down onto the Charvak reservoir
highlights.three: Mountain cafes, horse riding and open meadows in summer

charvak.title: Charvak reservoir
charvak.summary: A turquoise reservoir held between bare ochre ridges, an hour and a quarter out of the city and the shortest drive of the five. Swimming and boats from June through September, empty shorelines and remarkably clear air for the rest of the year.
charvak.photo: Charvak reservoir from an elevated viewpoint: intensely turquoise water surrounded by bare ochre mountains, a small boat wake crossing the frame, strong midday sun, deep blue sky, no people, 16:10 landscape.

photos.one: The turquoise Charvak reservoir seen from the ridge above, with a lakeside village and its bridge.
photos.two: The Charvak shoreline in summer — beach, boats and resort roofs under bare rock ridges.

highlights.one: The dam viewpoint over the length of the reservoir
highlights.two: Time on the shore — swimming and boat hire in summer
highlights.three: Lunch at a restaurant looking out over the water

chinorkent.title: Chinorkent cable car
chinorkent.summary: One of the most reliable and safest gondola lines in the world, and the one day of the four where the ride itself is the destination. The cabins are fully glazed, so the view is circular and uninterrupted from the moment you leave the lower station — close enough to the slope to feel part of it.
chinorkent.photo: A fully glazed panoramic gondola cabin crossing a wooded mountain gorge in the Western Tian Shan, plane trees and a river far below, layered ridges beyond, soft late-morning light, no people in frame, 16:10 landscape.

photos.one: The glass-fronted Chinorkent cable-car terminal below snow-covered peaks.
photos.two: A Chinorkent gondola cabin crossing the foothills above the town.

highlights.one: Fully glazed cabins with an uninterrupted circular view
highlights.two: A calm, unhurried crossing above the gorge and the pine slopes
highlights.three: Built and maintained to some of the strictest safety standards there are

tashkent-metro.title: Tashkent metro architecture
tashkent-metro.summary: The first metro in Central Asia, and one of the very few you would ride for the ceilings alone. Chandeliers, carved marble and cosmonaut mosaics thirty metres underground — and photography has only been officially allowed since 1 June 2018, which is why almost nobody outside the country has seen it.
tashkent-metro.photo: An ornate Tashkent metro station platform: domed ceiling with cosmonaut-themed mosaic medallions, blue tiled columns, hanging chandeliers, polished marble floor, symmetrical one-point perspective down the empty platform, no people, 16:10 landscape.

photos.one: The blue majolica domes of Alisher Navoi station on the Tashkent metro.
photos.two: A cosmonaut mosaic and crystal chandeliers under the vaulted ceiling of a Tashkent metro station.

highlights.one: Kosmonavtlar, Minor, Toshkent, Pakhtakor and Alisher Navoi
highlights.two: Cosmonaut medallions, domed mosaic halls and carved marble
highlights.three: Filming allowed since June 2018 — bring a camera

besh-qozon.title: Besh Qozon and the bazaars
besh-qozon.summary: Uzbekistan is known for plov, and Besh Qozon is where the country makes it at scale: roughly one and a half tonnes in a single day, out of open kazans wide enough to stand in. Afterwards we take you through the big bazaars, where the fruit rows are the part guests actually write to us about.
besh-qozon.photo: A close overhead shot of an Uzbek plov kazan: rice, carrot, chickpeas and lamb glistening under steam, a wooden serving spoon lifting a portion, warm tungsten market light, shallow depth of field, no faces in frame, 16:10 landscape.

photos.two: A cook turning plov in one of the giant kazans at Besh Qozon.
photos.three: The turquoise dome of Chorsu bazaar above the market rows of old Tashkent.

highlights.two: The big bazaars — spices, non bread, dried fruit and melons

magic-city.title: Magic City evening
magic-city.summary: The one route that starts after sunset. Magic City is a park built around a lake, with castle architecture that only really works in the dark, when the floodlights and the musical fountains come on. Walking the grounds costs nothing; the rides, the shows and the restaurants are what you pay for, and we will tell you which of them are worth it.
magic-city.photo: Magic City park in Tashkent after sunset: European castle-style pavilions under warm floodlight, their reflection in the lake, illuminated fountains mid-show, a lit promenade, deep blue evening sky, warm grading, no recognisable faces, 16:10 landscape.

photos.one: The illuminated castle at Magic City on a summer evening.
photos.two: The Magic City promenade and its balloon landmark under evening lights.

highlights.one: Castle architecture and the lake under floodlight after sunset
highlights.two: The musical fountain show, worth arriving before dark for
highlights.three: Free to walk in, so you only pay for the rides and the restaurants
